h: A pier that rose from the flames
p: The Grand Pier first opened in 1904, and it has a remarkable comeback story. In 2008 a huge fire destroyed the pavilion, and many people wondered if Weston would lose its favourite landmark. Instead, a brand new pavilion was built and the pier reopened in 2010, so today you get Edwardian heritage with a modern building at the end of it.

How long to spend depends on how much you want to do. A stroll out and back with an ice cream is a lovely hour, but add in rides, food and a mooch around the attractions and it can easily fill an afternoon. It's a handy plan for families who want a mix of sea air and indoor fun in the same outing.

A big tip for Weston: enjoy the sands, but keep well away from the mud. When the tide goes out, it leaves behind soft mud flats that can be genuinely dangerous to walk on. Stick to the firm sand closer to the promenade and keep an eye on little ones.

If you want to look further along the seafront, the old Birnbeck Pier stands at the northern end of the bay, a reminder of Weston's Victorian heyday. To the south, Brean Down is a National Trust headland with sweeping views over the Bristol Channel and an old fort to explore, perfect for a breezy walk. Cheddar Gorge and its caves are within an easy drive for a completely different kind of day.
Weston has its own railway station not far from the seafront, so you can leave the car at home and still reach the pier easily.
